long.q: Explain two strengths of using participant observation in sociological research.
scheme: B1: a strength: high validity / rich qualitative data
B1: explained: the researcher sees behaviour in its natural setting and from the group's point of view (verstehen)
B1: a second strength: access to hidden or deviant groups
B1: explained: trust built over time lets the researcher see what interviews would miss

long.q: Explain the difference between reliability and validity in research.
scheme: B1: reliability: research that can be repeated with the same results
B1: e.g. standardised methods such as structured questionnaires are more reliable
B1: validity: research that gives a true picture of what it set out to study
B1: e.g. qualitative methods such as unstructured interviews are often more valid
